Fairly large commit.  Mostly refactoring of chip8emu.

chip8emu has been refactored so that it contains only the things that deal
directly with the emulation of the instructions.  That means that
keyboard and display functionality have been moved out into their own
files. state for the display and keyboard are maintained in their own
structs, which the main chip8 struct contains.  Naturally the
CMakeLists.txt file has also been changed so that the project still
compiles correctly.

Another update to the emulation loop, and timer mechanism.

Timers are now internally represented as 16 bit registers that hold
values in milliseconds.  This makes updating them easier and
straightforward.

Also, timing for the ellapsed time between execution of operations
has changed.  Timing now starts AFTER the last instruction has been
executed for the current emulation loop, and ends right before the next
instruction in the following emulation loop.  This is important because
instructions that could potentially take a long time, like LD_Vx_K,
which hangs until a user presses a key, will cause the calculated
ellapsed time quite large, and will cause the emulator to execute a
large number of instrutions in succession.

TLDR: we are only measuring how long it takes the emulation loop to reach
the opcode execution time, and not including the time it takes to execute
said opcodes.

Changed emulation loop to only poll SDL events once per iteration.

This will ensure that execution doesn't hang if for some reason we get
a gigantic stream of events int at one time.
Small fixes.  Silenced a few CPU warnings.

Fixed emulation loop, to execute at a slower speed.

Explanation: Most (probably all) Chip8 program run at full Chip-8 speed.
The problem is that obviously a modern computer runs much faster, so we
need to artificially slow the emulation down.  At the moment, the emulator
executes 1 instruction every 2 ms giving a rate of just a bit under
512Hz. Note that this commit has removed the timer update functionality
for now.
